raw_response:
I will not spread my 5 mu too thin. My main money still comes from the wheat-maize rotation, because on irrigated land here that is the steadiest way to get grain. This year I will keep 3 mu in wheat followed by summer maize, then I will put 1 mu in peanut and 1 mu in cotton. I farm by looking at what worked before, but I also adjust a little. With well irrigation, I do not want to save too hard on fertilizer and then lose yield. Wheat and maize will get the heavier feeding because they carry the household grain and cash. Peanut fixes some nitrogen by itself, so I will put more emphasis on phosphorus and some potash. Cotton can eat fertilizer for a long season, but on just 1 mu I will control the cost and watch insects closely, because cotton without pest control is easy to lose. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it pays clearly, keep irrigation for the key stages, and do the field work in the simpler way when possible so I do not spend too much on labor.
